title: feat(scripts): derive what each pack-object importer reads off the pack, and how deep (objectui#9046)
body:
Fixes #9046

objectui#8752 made the pack-object importer LIST mechanical and stated, in the gate's own header, exactly what it was leaving behind: 「The list's **COMPLETENESS** is mechanical now (`derivePackObjectImporters()` plus its pin); what stays **hand-read** is what each importer's shape means.」 This PR derives that second clause. It adds no pin, changes neither existing leg, and wires nothing into CI.

## What the new leg derives, and how

Three functions, all additive:

- **`derivePackObjectPropertyReads(root, files)`** — resolves the local binding each pack import is bound to, from the **import clause** rather than by looking for the export's spelling. That matters on this tree: it already ships `en as enLocale`, `en as enPack` and a bare `en`, and a leg keyed on the export name would see one of the three. It then climbs every property chain read off that binding, stepping through `!`, parentheses and `as`, treating a string-literal index as the dot it is, and stopping at a **computed** access with `dynamic: true` rather than reporting the read as absent.
- **`packAliasesOf()`** (internal, resolved to a fixed point) — a local bound to a pack **subtree** is still a pack read. Without this the leg is defeated by a rename: `const g = en.deep.group;` then `g.leaf` spells no pack path anywhere. That edit reads as a tidy-up, which is how class 4 arrived in the first place. Deliberately narrow — only a `const` with a plain identifier name whose initializer is a static chain off a known root. A local initialised from a **function call** that returns a subtree is not resolved and cannot be; that needs types, not syntax.
- **`classifyPackObjectRead(read, packKeys, fileText)`** — resolves the chain against the pack's own leaf/branch split and **measures** which leg above can see it, by running this script's two boundary predicates over the importer's source.

The measurement is the part worth defending. Inferring coverage from the segment count (「three segments, so the property-chain leg has it」) is an inference about the **key**; what the leg needs is the probe's **text** to occur in a file. An alias read reaches a three-segment key while the file spells no leading dot at all — the inference says covered, the probe finds nothing. Running the predicate costs the same and cannot be wrong that way. A test pins exactly that divergence.

**Depth** is the load-bearing output, and the report says so: class 4 is precisely the shape where nothing but the depth separates a read both legs see from a read neither does.

## What it reports per real importer

Run on this branch's head over the five derived non-test importers — **22 reference rows across all five**, no importer silent:

| importer | what the instrument now says |
|:--|:--|
| `LoadingScreen.tsx` | one dynamically-indexed read of the locale-tag map (**opaque**, class 1), and four **subtree** reads — one at depth 1 over a namespace of 413 leaves, three at depth 2 over 3 / 4 / 2 leaves. No leg sees any of them. |
| `outboundAgentText.ts` | two depth-0 reads — both packs handed to a helper **whole**, as values. Opaque; the segments are not knowable from syntax. |
| `bulk-actions.tsx` | one depth-0 read — whole-pack `resources` wiring. Nothing for any leg to see. |
| `main.tsx` | ten depth-0 reads, one per locale, same whole-pack wiring. |
| `nonGridRowCeiling.tsx` | two **leaf** reads at **depth 2** — the class-4 shape, live. Reported as `seen by: full-key`, i.e. held out of the tiers **only** by the co-located literal spelling in the same expression. |

Two summary paragraphs follow the rows, and neither can go vacuous: the first reports the class-4 **shape** population (2) split by whether anything covers it (2 covered by coincidence, 0 dark) — so a tree with no instances and a tree held up entirely by co-located literals no longer render as the same silence. The second reports leaf reads no leg sees at **any** depth, which is where an alias read lands.

A subtree read is reported with the leaves it makes **reachable** and explicitly **not** as a liveness claim about any of them. Turning that row into one would mark a whole namespace live — the `wideHeads` mistake in another costume.

## It can fail, shown by invocation

This gate runs in no workflow (that is objectui#4658's ruling, and this PR does not touch it), so a CI colour would prove nothing. Both directions were run and read as **output**:

**Firing, on the real tree.** An ablation removed the co-located literal from the live instance — the `t()` call's literal key replaced by an identifier, the pack property read left exactly where it is, i.e. 「an edit that reads as a tidy-up」. The mutation was proved on disk before the run (literal first-arg occurrences `1 → 0` for both keys, injected markers present on both lines, the `en.common.rowCeiling…` reads confirmed unchanged). The gate's rows flipped from `seen by: full-key` to `NO LEG SEES THIS READ`, and the summary from 「2 … held visible ONLY by a co-located spelling … 0 are held by nothing at all」 to 「0 … 2 are held by nothing at all」. Restored by `git checkout HEAD -- ` on the path, proved by the file's blob hash matching its `HEAD` blob and by an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by an exit code.

**Silent when the shape is absent.** A fixture with no pack import produces no rows; a fixture with the shape **plus** a co-located literal keeps the row and reports it covered, rather than dropping it — a dropped row would render a property of that *file* as coverage by the *instrument*.

## What it still cannot see

Stated rather than discovered, because an under-reporting gate read as cleanliness is the harm the card is about.

1. **Class 4 is REPORTED, not CLOSED.** The leg reports the read; it does not make the key visible to the tiers. A key whose only reader is a two-segment property read still lands in CONFIRMED — the report now says, beside it, that a file reads it. What is gone is the silence, not the tiering. Where such a read names a key in CONFIRMED the CLI calls it a **wrong verdict** in those words; on this tree that line does not fire, and the reason is measured below.
2. **Class 5, newly named in the header: the subtree reader.** A file that takes a whole branch and reads leaves out of *that*. No probe can match, because no leaf is ever spelled, and the leaf is selected one hop past the pack binding — through a local whose contents need types rather than syntax to follow. This tree carries six such reads, together making 413 leaves reachable with none of them spelled. **This is the class that is measurably open.**
3. **Opaque reads stay opaque.** A computed index or a pack passed as a value: the leg says the segments are unknowable rather than reporting "reads nothing", which is the only honest output, not a fix.
4. **Function-returned subtrees.** `const strings = getStartupStrings()` is not an alias this walk can follow.
5. **No block scoping.** The alias map is file-scoped; a shadowed alias name would be attributed to the outer binding.

## Measured, and not taken

The wrong-verdict cross-reference stays silent on this tree, and not because the tree is clean where the card looks. Running the gate's own `analyze()`: the pack half collects three dynamic heads naming only a **top-level** namespace (`approvalsInbox.`, `common.`, `managedByBadge.`), and they hold **196** pack leaves out of the candidate set — 164 / 17 / 15 of them with no literal call site at all. The designer half of this same script **refuses** heads that wide, deletes them from the applied set and prints a loud line about it; the pack half neither filters nor reports. So the live instance's keys can never reach a tier regardless of what reads them.

⛔ Not taken here: narrowing the pack half's head leg is narrowing what an existing leg accepts, which objectui#9046 is fenced from. Filed bare as **objectui#9126** with the measurement.

## The typing follow-up (head `a5ca7cb49`)

`derivePackObjectKeyReads()` carried `@returns {Array<object>}`. An explicit `@returns` on an exported function **overrides inference for its callers**, so the pin test — which `tsconfig.scripts.json` does compile — read every row as `object` and each property access failed. Fixed at the source, ⛔ not by casting in the test and ⛔ not by loosening the tsconfig: three `@typedef`s (`PackObjectRead`, `PackObjectReadVerdict`, their intersection) now declare the derivation's public shape, and every exported function in the leg is annotated with them. The typedef block states in its own text why the shape is declared rather than inferred, so a field added to a row without being added there breaks callers with the reason written beside it. **Comment-only: zero executable lines changed, and the test file is untouched** (still 0 deletions, still 175 assertions).

## Untouched, verified

- The options-default switchboard line hashes to `496205d36d64614de4fa0e7497638c3c7a22feada9833cb481410d0f3e24e5d7` on this branch's head — unchanged.
- `ANALYSED_PACK_OBJECT_IMPORTERS` still holds 5 entries; objectui#8752's pin block is untouched. **0 lines deleted** from the test file; its assertions go 123 → 175, all additions.
- The key-boundary and property-boundary predicates appear in the diff only as **calls**; no `-` line touches either.
- **0** workflows reference this gate, before and after. `--strict` and the report-only `process.exit(0)` default are unchanged.

## Gates run, with their printed verdicts

| gate | verdict as printed |
|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` — exit 0. **No changeset is owed and none is added.** |
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` | `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 99 passed (99)` (76 → 99) |
| `vitest run scripts/` | `Test Files 143 passed, 2 skipped (145) · Tests 4271 passed, 2 skipped (4273)` (re-run after the typing fix: identical) |
| **`pnpm type-check:scripts`** (the command the required `Type Check` context runs) | **exit 0, no diagnostics.** `tsc` prints nothing on success, so the green is backed by a control rather than by silence: the same command on `4377016f7` exited **2** with **54** diagnostics, 53 TS2339 + 1 TS7006, every one in this PR's test file — so the file is demonstrably in the program. `tsc --listFiles` confirms it directly: 915 files, both changed files among them. |
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/scripts-type-check.test.ts` | `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 15 passed (15)` — ⚠️ a test **about** the type-check wiring, **not** the type-check command. Listing it as the type-check gate is what let the red above through; it is kept here only so the distinction is on the record. |
| `check:control-bytes` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 7318 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `check:new-line-citations` | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `check:entry-guard` | `✓ check:entry-guard: 89 scripts/ file(s) — no entry guard outside the baseline` |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | exit 0, report read in full — the new section is the evidence above |
| `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two changed files | 0 errors, 0 warnings |

On lint scope: the repo's lint gate is `turbo run lint` (per-package), not a root-wide `eslint .`. A root-wide run was done anyway for the invariance reading — 4801 files, both changed files at 0/0, and the 95 errors it reports sit in 79 files under `apps/`, `e2e/` and `packages/`, none of them in this diff. `eslint.config.js` enables neither `projectService` nor `parserOptions.project`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.
